scores.note: One-character change: adds the missing newline to an asynPrint ASYN_TRACE_ERROR message in devMotorAsyn.c init_record (pasynGenericPointer->read failure path). Cosmetic log defect only; the error path is not reachable in the sim IOC so this was read, not executed. Applies with offset 7 lines, builds, no new warnings. No effect on consumers.

One line in check_speed_and_resolution (called from init_record only): HVEL==0 now defaults to VELO instead of VBAS. Executed with the real motorSim IOC (motorSim built against pin libmotor and against pin+F2 libmotor), asyn motor record with HVEL unset: with VBAS=0 the pin leaves HVEL=0 and a HOMF does nothing (DMOV stays 1, RBV stays 0); with F2 HVEL=1 and the axis homes at about 0.6 EGU/s. With VBAS=0.1 pin homes at about 0.12 EGU/s, F2 about 1.2 EGU/s (about 10x). Real functional bug for the common VBAS=0 default, but it is also a behaviour change after restart (homing speed rises from VBAS to VELO) so regression surface is not zero. pmac basic_asyn_motor.template sets HVEL 0 and pmacAxis::home sends '#n HOME' ignoring the velocity arguments, so pmac motion is unaffected; motorMotorSim db sets HVEL=1 explicitly.

pseudoMotor.db only: grecord->record, tabs->spaces, and C1..C5 VAL now $(C1=1)..$(C5=1). Verified with base msi on the installed real files: pin ignores C1=3,C3=7 (VAL stays 1); patched gives 3 and 7, and with no macros all VAL are 1, so it is backward compatible. The rest of the diff is whitespace noise (a diff ignoring leading blanks shows only the 5 VAL lines). Could not load the db in an IOC (motorSim has no transform record or Soft Channel device support), so only macro expansion was run. Nothing in pmac-src or motorMotorSim-src references pseudoMotor.db. Leaf template, no C/C++ change.

New feature (position compare output), no fix. 05b25c1 adds five asyn parameters and virtual asynMotorAxis::enablePCO (base returns asynSuccess), changes the asynMotorController class layout (ABI change, every driver must rebuild), and REMOVES LAST_MOTOR_PARAM and NUM_MOTOR_DRIVER_PARAMS. pmac 2-7-9 uses NUM_MOTOR_DRIVER_PARAMS in pmacController.cpp:137 and pmacCSController.cpp:151: built against pin the pmacController objects and libpmacAsynMotorPort.so build; built against patched motor both files fail with 'NUM_MOTOR_DRIVER_PARAMS was not declared'. The group also adds about 24000 lines of operator screens (adl, bob, edl, opi, ui) that nothing in the build uses. Runtime: in the sim IOC with the patched libmotor, positionCompare.template writes/readbacks work (Start, End, Increment, PulseWidth, Enable, EGU microsec), but nothing implements PCO (motorSim and pmac do not), so no function results. Template on pin: 'cannot find parameter PCO_*'. Low value, highest regression and blast radius in the set.

One line in check_speed_and_resolution (motorRecord.cc): HVEL==0 now becomes VELO instead of VBAS, mirroring the existing JVEL rule. Ran real IOC (motorSim, libmotor from pin vs pin+F2, HVEL left at 0 as in basic_asyn_motor.db): pin gives HVEL=0 for VBAS=0 and HOMF does not move the axis (RBV stays 0); pin gives HVEL=VBAS=0.1 for VBAS=0.1 and homes at 0.1 mm/s; with F2 both give HVEL=VELO=1 and home at about 1 mm/s (RBV +0.6 per 0.5 s read pair, 10x faster for the VBAS=0.1 axis). So it fixes a no-move home for default-DB motors but is a behavior change, not a pure bug fix: it raises default homing speed. Consumer risk (code read, not run, no PMAC hardware): pmacAxis::home treats max_velocity==0 as 'use the controller Ix23 home speed' and overrides it with max_velocity/1000 when non-zero; pmac basic_asyn_motor.template sets HVEL=0 and VBAS default 0, so with F2 every pmac axis would home at VELO instead of the controller-configured speed, with limits disabled during some home types. Core record file (motorRecord.cc), reaches every motor record; applies clean, builds with no new warning.

pseudoMotor.db only: C1-C5 VAL becomes $(Cn=1), default 1 preserves behavior; also grecord->record and tab-to-space reindent (diff is 142 lines, but content change is the 5 VAL lines). Ran real softIoc from EPICS Base loading the C1-C5 stanzas taken verbatim from the installed pseudoMotor.db of pin and pin+F3: pin gives C1..C5 = 1 even with C1=3,C2=4,C5=9.5 passed; F3 gives 1 1 1 1 1 by default and 3 4 1 1 9.5 with macros. Full pseudoMotor.db could not be loaded in the motorSim IOC (no 'motor' Soft Channel device support and no transform record type in that dbd; same error in pin and F3), so the whole-file load is unverified. No file in motorMotorSim-src or pmac-src references pseudoMotor.db. Applies clean, no compiled code, no ABI effect; leaf template.

Whole group of six commits: positionCompare.template + settings.req, five PCO asyn parameters and a virtual asynMotorAxis::enablePCO (base class is an empty asynSuccess stub) wired into asynMotorController::writeInt32, plus about 24000 diff lines of generated adl/bob/edl/opi/ui screens. 05b25c1 also deletes LAST_MOTOR_PARAM, NUM_MOTOR_DRIVER_PARAMS and the asyn<4.32 branch. Ran real motorSim IOC with the real template: with the pin libmotor the template records get 'cannot find parameter PCO_*' and read back 0; with patched libmotor the writes round-trip (Start 1.5, End 9, Inc 0.25, Width 20 microsec, Enable). But no driver in this environment overrides enablePCO (grep of pmac-src and motorMotorSim-src), so PCOEnable does nothing on hardware; pmac has its own positionCompare.vdb. Breaks the pmac consumer at compile time (NUM_MOTOR_DRIVER_PARAMS removed, used in pmacController.cpp:137 and pmacCSController.cpp:151); adds virtual and data members to exported classes (ABI break, every driver must be rebuilt). Large, core-header touching, no facility benefit today, and the one real consumer breaks.

scores.note: One-character change: adds \n to an asynPrint ERROR string in devMotorAsyn.c init_record (read-failure path). Cosmetic log defect only, rare path, no behavior change. Patch applies with 7-line offset, no fuzz.

One line in check_speed_and_resolution (motorRecord.cc), called only from init_record: HVEL==0 now defaults to VELO, not VBAS. Run test with real libmotor + motorSim (3 axes, home at 50 mm): pin gives HVEL=0.5 for VBAS=0.5 and HVEL=0 for VBAS=0; with VBAS=0 the home command is a silent no-op (RBV stays 0, DMOV=1 at 4 s and 12 s). With F2 HVEL=VELO=2 for both, both axes home (RBV 7.6 at 4 s, 23.6 at 12 s); explicit HVEL=1.5 unchanged (identical in both). So it fixes a real functional hole for the very common VBAS=0 default, matching the existing JVEL default to VELO. Cost: sites with HVEL unset and VBAS>0 will home at VELO (faster) after the change, a behavior change on real hardware; workaround without patch is to set HVEL explicitly in the db. Core record file but one init-only line; clean apply, same warnings.

Only motorApp/Db/pseudoMotor.db: grecord->record, tabs to spaces, and VAL of C1..C5 from "1" to "$(Cn=1)". Executed real msi on pin and patched file: no macros gives five VAL="1" in both; C1=2.5,C3=7 gives 2.5 and 7 (others 1) only with F3; whitespace/grecord-normalized diff with defaults is identical. Default-compatible, db-only leaf, no C++ and no build effect (installed db differs only in whitespace). 142-line diff is mostly re-indent. Value is low: neither motorMotorSim nor pmac references pseudoMotor.db; only helps sites that template pseudo-motor constants. Full pseudoMotor.db could not be loaded in an IOC because transform record support is not in the available test IOC; load of the motor records was not exercised.

Feature, not a fix: adds PCO_* asyn params, virtual asynMotorAxis::enablePCO (base is a no-op returning asynSuccess), a positionCompare.template/.req and operator screens; 05b25c1 also deletes the pre-4.32 asyn branch and the macros LAST_MOTOR_PARAM and NUM_MOTOR_DRIVER_PARAMS. Run test (motorSim linked to real patched libmotor): template records create and round-trip (start 1.5, end 9, incr 0.25, width 20 microsec, enable) but nothing acts on them since no driver in this environment overrides enablePCO. Removing NUM_MOTOR_DRIVER_PARAMS breaks pmac: pmacController.cpp:137 and pmacCSController.cpp:151 fail with 'NUM_MOTOR_DRIVER_PARAMS was not declared'. Also changes the asynMotorController/asynMotorAxis class layout and vtable (new virtual, new int members), so every driver must be rebuilt, and the numParams constructor argument becomes ignored. 24k-line patch, mostly operator screens. Best skipped until the bump (with a matching pmac update).

scores.note: One-character change: appends \n to the asynPrint format string in devMotorAsyn.c init_record, on the error path of the initial pasynGenericPointer->read. Without it a failed read prints an unterminated trace line that runs into the next message. Compiled libmotor.so checked at byte level: pin has 'read returned %s\0', fix has 'read returned %s\n\0'. No logic change, no consumer impact, leaf file. Failure path not reachable on motorSim, so the runtime effect was read from code only.

One line in check_speed_and_resolution: HVEL==0 now defaults to VELO instead of VBAS. Run on real motorSim IOC (motorSimSupport built against pin vs pin+F2, basic_asyn_motor.db, VELO=2): with VBAS=0.1 the pin homes at about 0.12 EGU/s (HVEL read back 0.1), the fix at about 2.4 EGU/s (HVEL read back 2). With VBAS=0 the pin leaves HVEL=0 and HOMF ends immediately after a 0.1 jump (home never really runs), the fix homes normally. So it fixes a real functional defect for the common VBAS=0 setup, and aligns HVEL with JVEL (which already defaults to VELO). Costs: changes documented behaviour (docs/motor_release.html says HVEL is set to VBAS; fix does not update it), and homing at full VELO instead of VBAS is a behaviour change every site relying on HVEL=0 gets. pmac sends '#n HOME' and ignores the velocity, so pmac is unaffected; pmac's template sets HVEL=0. Applies clean (no offset), builds with identical warnings. Core record file, so locality is middling, but the change is one line.

pseudoMotor.db only: C1..C5 VAL becomes $(C1=1)..$(C5=1) with default 1, grecord renamed record, tabs turned into 4 spaces (142-line diff, mostly whitespace). msi expansion of the real installed file with the default macros, pin vs fix, is identical modulo grecord/record and whitespace (diff -w), and C1=5,C3=2.5 give VAL 5 and 2.5 in the fix while the pin stays at 1. Backward compatible. Useful only for sites that load pseudoMotor.db with their own constants; neither pmac nor motorMotorSim references it. Could not load the file into a running IOC because the transform record type is not in the motorSim build; msi expansion only. Builds, same install file set as pin.

Group of six commits adding position compare output (PCO): new template, base class asynMotorAxis::enablePCO (virtual no-op), five PCO parameters on asynMotorController, and operator screens. Built singly and as a group, libmotor and libsoftMotor build with warnings identical to the pin. Run on motorMotorSim IOC (sim built against pin+F4, positionCompare.template loaded): PCO_* parameters exist (asynReport params 76-80), setpoints echo to _RBV, PCOEnable writes reach the base no-op; nothing happens in hardware because no driver in this environment overrides enablePCO. DEFECT for consumers: 05b25c1 deletes LAST_MOTOR_PARAM and NUM_MOTOR_DRIVER_PARAMS; pmac 2-7-9 uses NUM_MOTOR_DRIVER_PARAMS in pmacController.cpp:137 and pmacCSController.cpp:151, and libpmacAsynMotorPort no longer compiles against the F4-patched motor (error: NUM_MOTOR_DRIVER_PARAMS was not declared in this scope; pin builds it with exit 0). Also changes the asynMotorController class layout (new members), so every driver must be rebuilt. New feature, not a fix; no urgency; deep base-class header with breaking symbol removal.

defects.description: 05b25c1 removes the NUM_MOTOR_DRIVER_PARAMS and LAST_MOTOR_PARAM macros without a compatibility definition. pmac 2-7-9 (pmacController.cpp:137, pmacCSController.cpp:151) passes NUM_MOTOR_DRIVER_PARAMS to asynMotorController; built pmacApp/src against pin+F4: 'error: NUM_MOTOR_DRIVER_PARAMS was not declared in this scope' (both files); same source against the pin builds. The pmac module in this environment would stop building if F4 were carried.

positionCompare.template (8cec391) sets field(ZSV) twice in PCOEnable_RBV and has no ONSV/ZSV mapping as apparently intended (second ZSV looks like it should be ONSV); the db still loads (last duplicate wins). PCOEnable has no PINI so the enable state is not initialised from the record. enablePCO is a base-class no-op returning asynSuccess, so a driver that lacks an override silently reports success.

Not a code defect, but the fix changes behaviour documented in docs/motor_release.html (HVEL set to VBAS when uninitialised) and the commit does not touch the documentation; homing speed for every HVEL=0 record rises from VBAS to VELO.

scores.note: One-character fix (missing \n) in an asynPrint ERROR message in devMotorAsyn.c init_record. Run: motorSim IOC with a motor record at an invalid ADDR (3 of 1 axis). Pin prints '...readGenericPointer Invalid axis 32026/10/30 ...init_controller...' (two log lines fused, no newline); with F1 the lines are separate. Only fires on an init failure path; no behavior change. Applies clean (offset 7), builds with identical warnings, no consumer touches it.

One line in check_speed_and_resolution: HVEL==0 now defaults to VELO instead of VBAS. Run: motorSim IOC, VELO=1 VBAS=0.1 HVEL unset: pin HVEL=0.1, patched HVEL=1 (dbgf). Real bug case: with VBAS=0 (record default) pin leaves HVEL=0, and the home code (motorRecord.cc ~861,2047) then sends velocity 0. Consumers: pmacAxis::home ignores the velocity args (sends '#n HOME'), though pmac basic_asyn_motor.template sets HVEL=0 so the field value changes; motorSimTest.db sets HVEL=1 explicitly. So little effect on our consumers. Regression surface: every record with HVEL unset now homes at VELO (faster) on drivers that honor it; the record core is touched but only at init. Applies clean, builds clean.

pseudoMotor.db only: C1-C5 VAL becomes $(Cn=1) (default preserved), grecord->record, tabs->spaces. Run: mini IOC (motor, softMotor, calc, asyn) loading the real installed pseudoMotor.db with C1=7,C3=2.5: patched C1..C5 = 7,1,2.5,1,1; with no macros all 1; pin ignores the macros (all 1). Feature/convenience, not a defect fix. No consumer (motorMotorSim, pmac) references pseudoMotor.db (grep). Clean apply, db-only so no compile effect, no file overlap with other fixes.

Group of 6 commits (30 files, ~24k diff lines: template, req, 05b25c1 C++ changes, adl/bob/edl/opi/ui screens). Adds PCO asyn params and virtual asynMotorAxis::enablePCO (base no-op). Run: motorSim controller with the real positionCompare.template: patched libmotor serves PCO params and round-trips values (EGU microsec); pin libmotor gives 'cannot find parameter PCO_*' for all 10 records. But no driver of ours implements PCO: only PCOEnable reaches enablePCO (no-op), the other four values just sit in the parameter library. Harmful side: 05b25c1 deletes NUM_MOTOR_DRIVER_PARAMS and LAST_MOTOR_PARAM, and pmac 2-7-9 uses NUM_MOTOR_DRIVER_PARAMS in pmacController.cpp:137 and pmacCSController.cpp:151 -> pmac fails to compile against patched motor (verified). asynMotorController class layout and the axis vtable change: motorSim binary built against the pin segfaults when run on patched libmotor (verified), so all drivers must be rebuilt. Low value for the facility, high regression surface, deep-core header change.

defects.description: 05b25c1 removes NUM_MOTOR_DRIVER_PARAMS (and LAST_MOTOR_PARAM) from asynMotorController.h; pmac 2-7-9 pmacApp/src/pmacController.cpp:137 and pmacCSController.cpp:151 still use it. Reproduced: make -k of pmac against patched motor gives 'error: NUM_MOTOR_DRIVER_PARAMS was not declared in this scope' in both files; same tree against the pin compiles those files.

Binary incompatibility: 05b25c1 adds 5 int members to asynMotorController and a virtual to asynMotorAxis. motorSim built on the pin crashes (Segmentation fault) with the patched libmotor, so every driver module must be rebuilt together with motor.

PCO is only plumbing: enablePCO is a base no-op and start/end/increment/pulse width have no virtual hook, so no driver in this environment (motorSim, pmac) acts on them; records show success without any effect.

Template/req nits: positionCompare.template PCOEnable_RBV sets ZSV twice (no OSV pairing for the first), PCOEnable has no PINI, and positionCompare_settings.req uses $(R) while the template and other req files key on $(P)$(M).

Behavior change not a pure fix: records with HVEL unset now home at VELO rather than VBAS on drivers that use the velocity (motorSim); pmac ignores it. Verified only at init (check_speed_and_resolution), later VELO changes do not update an auto-defaulted HVEL.
